rules.rationale: Highly electronegative halogen anions give deep localized valence bands and the widest experimental gaps among known compounds.
Main-group oxides lack partially filled d bands, so no mid-gap d states narrow the O 2p to cation s separation.
Sulfides, selenides and tellurides are polarizable covalent semiconductors clustering at the narrow-gap end of the pool.
Low mean Z implies compact valence orbitals, weak spin-orbit coupling, and larger bonding-antibonding splitting.

skills.hypothesis: Ionicity and closed d shells rank wide-gap insulators; the large chalcogenide penalty replaces the narrow pnictide rule to steer away from a bigger narrow-gap block. Fails if pool oxides are mixed-valence.

rules.rationale: Source halides suppress refractive index (-3.33); under the Moss relation low polarizability implies wide experimental gaps.
Metalloid dominance carried the largest source index effect (+9.23), inverting to polarizable narrow-gap semiconducting chemistry.
Heavy-atom source index gain (+6.07) reflects loose valence electrons, which shrink the fundamental band gap.
Source confidence only 0.024, so this uncertain relation is downweighted to a near-neutral guard.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers source refractive-index effects with reversed sign under the Moss relation while shrinking the lowest-confidence relations. Fails if source signs carry no transferable information or target gaps are defect- and structure-driven.

state.lesson: Across two development generations the domain-chemistry skill held a higher mean AUC (70.3 then 69.8) than the Moss-inverted transfer (65.2 then 61.4), though the inverted skill reached higher mean final best, suggesting it explores usefully but ranks poorly early. Both skills still collapse on a minority of seeds, so no causal claim is made from eight-seed summaries; the revision keeps first-principles ionicity as the deployed ranking and trims the weakest source relations rather than discarding the transfer.
state.revision_summary: Reformatted every conditions block as a field-to-value object to satisfy the schema. Deployed skill keeps halogen and d0-oxide rules, replaces the small pnictide penalty with a broader chalcogenide covalency penalty covering a much larger narrow-gap block, and slightly lowers semantic mass and prior scale to reduce seed collapses. The counter-hypothesis retains Moss-inverted source effects (halide positive, metalloid and high mean Z negative) with the lowest-confidence transition-metal relation shrunk to -0.2. Source evidence values are unchanged; no target outcomes or candidate identifiers are used.
